item.text: I’m checking for election-specific 2024 reporting and then I’ll confine the note to claim-level positives and negatives tied to 4B.3.

item.text:
**Assessment**: mostly no. The best 2024 evidence is a narrow procedural positive around specific rerun elections and observer access, but the broader record shows arrests of opposition figures and journalists, emergency-law repression, restrictions on social media and assemblies, and a closed civic-space environment.

- **Freedom in the World 2025 Country Report** | Freedom House | 2025 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/ethiopia/freedom-world/2025 | The report says Abiy-era electoral-law and NEBE reforms improved electoral operations and encouraged more opposition participation, and that some June 2024 legislative/regional elections were peaceful and credible according to AU observers. This is the strongest positive evidence for tolerating some contestation and monitoring, but it is limited to procedure. | `4B.3`, `4B.1`, `4B.2`
- **Final Observation Report on the Outstanding and Reelections of the Sixth General Elections Held in Benishangul Gumuz, Afar, Somali and Central Ethiopia Regions in June 24 2024** | CECOE | 2024 | https://cecoe.org/download/final-observation-report-on-the-outstanding-and-reelections-of-the-sixth-general-elections-held-in-benishangul-gumuz-afar-somali-and-central-ethiopia-regions-in-june-24-2024/ | Domestic observers described the June 24 reruns as transparent enough for systematic observation, with broad observer deployment and monitoring of polling, counting, and the post-election environment. This supports a narrow positive reading on monitoring access, but only for limited rerun elections. | `4B.3`, `4B.1`
- **World Report 2024: Ethiopia** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-12 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/ethiopia | HRW said authorities harassed and detained critical voices, tightly controlled reporting, restricted social media, and arrested opposition figures and journalists. This is direct evidence against tolerance for criticism, investigative journalism, and protest. | `4B.3`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`
- **Ethiopia’s Deepening Crackdown on Dissent** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-03-04 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/04/ethiopias-deepening-crackdown-dissent | HRW reported detentions of an opposition spokesperson and a journalist, plus broad arbitrary detention under emergency powers. This is strong evidence that the government did not tolerate criticism or dissent in practice. | `4B.3`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`
- **Ethiopia: Journalist arrested under state of emergency: Belay Manaye** | Amnesty International | 2024-03-14 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/afr25/7782/2024/en/ | Amnesty said a journalist was detained under emergency powers for reporting on the Amhara conflict, and that other journalists had also been arbitrarily arrested under the state of emergency. This is direct evidence against tolerance for investigative journalism. | `4B.3`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`
- **Ethiopia - CIVICUS Monitor** | CIVICUS Monitor | 2024-12-04 | https://monitor.civicus.org/press_release/2024/ethiopia/ | CIVICUS downgraded Ethiopia’s civic space to “Closed,” citing surveillance, harassment, intimidation, and threats against journalists and opposition members. That is strong evidence against tolerating protest or civil-society monitoring. | `4B.3`, `3B.8`
- **Ethiopia authorities suspend three rights groups** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-12-02 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/02/ethiopia-authorities-suspend-three-rights-groups | HRW said the government suspended three rights groups even as Abiy praised reforms like media freedom and NGO registration. The operational result was selective punishment of civic monitors, not tolerance. | `4B.3`, `3B.8`, `4B.2`

**Search gap**
- I did not find a 2024 primary-source statement from Abiy clearly accepting adverse election outcomes, open criticism, or independent civil-society monitoring as a binding constraint on his rule.
- The best pro-tolerance evidence is procedural and localized, not broad. It shows some observer access and some rerun elections, but it does not offset the larger pattern of repression.
